clue.text: Pity poor State representative

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters of the word pity are knocked into a new order

parts.note: CAL is a short form of California, a US state

explanation.surface: A pitiful governor is being described as a sorry figure for their state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges PITY into TYPI; CAL then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something representative is characteristic of its kind, a standard example.

clue.text: Pipit — the offspring of two birds

parts.note: the tit is a small common songbird
the lark is a songbird famous for singing in flight

explanation.surface: A bird is described as the chick of a cross between two other species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the offspring of' just says the answer is born of the two birds joined together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit is a small brown songbird, and this name is used for one species of it.

clue.text: A lot of wine, ideal for producing a reverie

parts.note: a pipe is a large cask of wine, about 105 gallons
an ideal, a perfect thing, can be called a dream

explanation.surface: Drinking plenty of wine is the perfect way to drift into daydreams.
explanation.walkthrough: A PIPE is an old measure of wine, a big barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful hope that will never come true is a daydream or idle reverie.

clue.text: Many on ship would constitute this

definitions.text: Many on ship would constitute this

parts.words: Many on ship would constitute this
parts.note: many things carried aboard a vessel together make up its freight

explanation.surface: A large crowd aboard a vessel would make up something.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods loaded on a ship as a whole form its freight.

clue.text: Does not include signs of Spring

definitions.meaning: to omit something is to exclude it
foliage appearing on trees shows that spring has arrived

explanation.walkthrough: The page carries the last word, Spring, over to the next column.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to exclude; and foliage sprouting on trees in spring shows the season has come.

clue.text: The best grannie makes a bow?

parts.note: the top is the highest or best
a granny knot is a common, insecure knot, so grannie stands for a knot

explanation.surface: An excellent grandmother is said to make a fine bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grannie' is the granny knot, not a grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a ribbon tied in a decorative loop on top of the head.

clue.text: Builds up first-rate section of bone

indicators.note: in a down clue building something up means writing it from the bottom upwards, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the 1 written as the letter I
a bit is a section or piece

explanation.surface: Something first-class is built up as part of a skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Builds up' reverses AI + BIT, giving the run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The shinbone is the larger of the two bones of the lower leg.

clue.text: Energy cycles?

parts.note: bicycles driven by human effort rather than an engine, effort being push

explanation.surface: Something about the recurring rhythms of power.
explanation.walkthrough: Push is energy and bikes are cycles, but the whole reads as one cryptic idea: bicycles you power yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal bicycle, as opposed to a motorbike, is one moved by the rider's own push.

clue.text: Measures in hand may be cut

definitions.meaning: a nail was an old cloth measure of two and a quarter inches
the horny tips of the fingers get trimmed

explanation.definitionFit: Old cloth units of length; and fingertips' horny plates, which one trims.

clue.text: Device enabling climbers to be trained

definitions.text: Device enabling climbers to be trained

parts.words: Device enabling climbers to be trained
parts.note: climbers here are climbing plants, guided up a framework

explanation.surface: A piece of gear lets mountaineers be coached.
explanation.walkthrough: Climbers are plants, not mountaineers, and training is guiding their growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice framework of wood on which climbing plants are grown.

clue.text: Make light of record run

parts.note: to tape something is to record it
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a record-breaking run.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a thin candle or wick used to give a flame.

clue.text: First-class in a function for resisting the heat

indicators.note: in places the first-class word inside the a-and-function pair

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
best means first-class

explanation.surface: An excellent performance at a function keeps out the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: BEST goes inside A SINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestine means made of or like asbestos, so fireproof and incombustible.

clue.text: A woman of star quality — and the city law officer

parts.note: Rome is the Eternal City
DA is a District Attorney, a US law officer

explanation.surface: A glamorous actress is paired with an urban attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star quality' hints that she is also a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The princess of Greek myth, rescued by Perseus, gives her name to a constellation.

clue.text: He was put in the pot by Isabella

definitions.text: He was put in the pot by Isabella

parts.words: He was put in the pot by Isabella
parts.note: Keats's poem Isabella; here the herb is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man is cooked by a woman called Isabella.
explanation.walkthrough: The herb doubles as a man's name, hence 'He'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic herb, in Keats's poem grown in a pot over Lorenzo's buried head.

clue.text: Sounds like Charlie's girl

definitions.note: verb: a bell sounds, or tolls

indicators.note: like says the girl's name is said aloud

parts.note: Little Nell is the heroine of Charles Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: A voice resembles that of Charlie's girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is Charles Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: To toll is to ring a bell slowly, as for a death.

clue.text: Number one in show business?

parts.note: the leading figure in London's annual ... Show procession

explanation.surface: A question about the top star of entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lord Mayor's Show is a yearly parade in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The civic head of the City of London stars in the procession named after the office.

clue.text: Fringe area where slacks are presumably worn

definitions.text: Fringe area where slacks are presumably worn

parts.words: Fringe area where slacks are presumably worn
parts.note: jokingly, a place where trousers are worn in place of skirts

explanation.surface: Somewhere on the edge, people go about in trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the word as 'out skirts': skirts out, slacks in.
explanation.definitionFit: The edges of a town lie beyond its centre.

clue.text: Lead from table has several bridge players in a state

indicators.note: the lead from a word is its first letter

parts.note: the bridge players sit at the compass points: E, N, N, E, S, S, E, E

explanation.surface: Leading a card from the table, the card players sit in some state.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state of the southeast, home of Nashville.

clue.text: Sort of ruler and a parish bigwig

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to sort out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of measuring stick is paired with a parish VIP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges RULER AND A.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric supervising a group of parishes in the Church of England.

clue.text: Marian sat out to get a thoughtful fellow

indicators.note: out signals the letters being put out of order

explanation.surface: Marian sat aside to find a considerate man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MARIAN SAT.
explanation.definitionFit: From the parable, a Good Samaritan is someone who kindly helps strangers.

clue.text: Unacceptable in a sensible garment for the clergy

indicators.note: in places the unacceptable word inside the sensible word

parts.note: sane means sensible
out means not acceptable, as in 'that's out'

explanation.surface: Unfit for sensible clerical clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassock worn by Roman Catholic priests.

clue.text: Shoots back — it's the end of a character

indicators.note: back tells you the word for shoots is written in reverse

parts.note: fires means shoots a gun

explanation.surface: A gunman fires in return, and a figure is finished off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses FIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stroke finishing the arm of a printed letter.

clue.text: False praise for fools at the wicket

definitions.meaning: Kipling's 'flannelled fools at the wicket' are cricketers in white woollen trousers

explanation.walkthrough: Kipling mocked cricketers as flannelled fools; flannel is their clothing cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty flattery; and the woollen cloth of cricketers' whites.

clue.text: Remove weapons from lunar module assembly

indicators.note: from tells you the answer is taken out of the run of words lunar module

explanation.surface: Weapons are stripped from the moon-landing craft.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone is to take their arms away.

clue.text: Grant a court charge

parts.note: a ward of court is a child in the court's charge

explanation.surface: A judge is asked to approve a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something formally, as a prize or damages.

clue.text: Argue madly about water supply — it's irregular

indicators.note: about puts the scrambled word round the water supply
madly says the letters of argue go wild

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Disputing wildly over the plumbing, someone behaves oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' turns ARGUE into GUERA, split around RILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is an irregular fighter outside a regular army; 'irregular' is a noun here.

clue.text: Up in arms — it makes one see red

definitions.text: Up in arms — it makes one see red

parts.words: Up in arms — it makes one see red
parts.note: versed in coats of arms, one knows this tincture means red

explanation.surface: Angry protest is infuriating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in arms' means versed in heraldry, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic name for the colour red.

clue.text: Walker coming up to run over old ground

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a pacer is a horse or person that walks at a set pace

explanation.surface: A hiker approaching revisits a familiar route.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise is to go back over what was said.

clue.text: Lily, Milton's sporty girl

definitions.meaning: a bulb plant with lily-like flowers
Milton's Lycidas speaks of 'to sport with ... in the shade'

explanation.definitionFit: A showy flowering plant; and the nymph Milton pictured being sported with in the shade.

clue.text: Innocent with money to spare

parts.note: C is short for cent, a small coin
spare and lean both mean thin

explanation.surface: A guiltless person has cash left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Blameless, with no record of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Survives being badly nursed by sweetheart

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter

indicators.note: badly says the letters of nursed are put wrong

explanation.surface: A patient pulls through despite poor care from a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges NURSED as NDURES; 'by' puts E beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To last or hold out through hardship.

clue.text: Men pale, when wrongly put on jury

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of men pale are arranged incorrectly

explanation.surface: Men go white when wrongly sworn as jurors.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol people on a panel, especially a jury.
